Adeia names Dipti Vachani as new CEO, effective Oct. 12

# Adeia names Dipti Vachani as new CEO, effective Oct. 12

September 28, 2026 4:05 PM EDT

Adeia Inc. (Nasdaq: ADEA) has appointed Dipti Vachani as chief executive officer, effective October 12, 2026. Vachani will also join the company's board of directors on the same date, according to a company statement.

Vachani succeeds Paul E. Davis, who informed the company in May 2026 of his intention to step down as CEO and board member to focus on his health. Davis will serve in an advisory capacity through the end of 2026 to support the transition.

Vachani most recently served as senior vice president and general manager of the Automotive Business Unit at Arm Limited, a role she held from 2018 to 2026. Prior to Arm, she served as vice president and general manager of Intel Corporation's Internet of Things Group from 2015 to 2018. She also held a vice president and general manager role at Skyworks Solutions beginning in 2013, and previously held various positions at Texas Instruments, Inc., ending as vice president and general manager of Single Core Processors.

Vachani served on the board of directors of Axcelis Technologies, Inc. from 2022 to 2025. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering from Texas A&M University and an Executive M.B.A. from the University of Texas at Austin.

"The Board's Transition Committee conducted a rigorous search process and considered an exceptional field of candidates," said Dan Moloney, chairman of the board.

"Adeia's award-winning portfolio of more than 14,250 worldwide patent assets, its deep culture of invention, and the momentum the team has built provide a remarkable foundation for the company's future," Vachani said in the statement.

San Jose, California-based Adeia licenses semiconductor and media technology innovations to companies across chip design and manufacturing, consumer electronics, automotive, digital entertainment, and e-commerce industries.

Beginning October 12, Vachani’s annual base salary is $730,000, with a target bonus equal to 100% of salary based on company financial objectives and individual objectives set by the Board; her fiscal 2026 bonus will be prorated for her active employment. Her equity awards have an aggregate target grant date value of $11,000,000: $4,400,000 in time-based restricted stock units vesting over four years and $6,600,000 in performance-based units tied to a three-year performance period and continued employment. For qualifying terminations, the planned severance agreement provides cash equal to 150% of salary plus target bonus if the termination is more than three months before or more than twelve months after a change in control, and 200% if it is within three months before or twelve months following one.

# Adeia Appoints Dipti Vachani as Chief Executive Officer

 By: Adeia Inc. via GlobeNewswire 

September 28, 2026 at 16:05 PM EDT

SAN JOSE, Calif., Sept. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Adeia Inc. (Nasdaq: ADEA), the technology company pioneering foundational innovations that shape how the world computes, connects, and experiences entertainment, today announced that its board of directors (the “Board”) has appointed Dipti Vachani as chief executive officer, effective October 12, 2026. Vachani will also join the Board, effective the same day. She succeeds Paul E. Davis, who in May 2026 informed the company of his intention to step down as chief executive officer and member of the Board to focus on his health and personal pursuits. Davis has agreed to serve in an advisory capacity through the end of the year to support a smooth transition.

Vachani brings to Adeia a tremendous wealth of broad leadership experience, technical credibility and meaningful partnerships, developed over nearly 30 years in the semiconductor industry. She has deep expertise in semiconductor ecosystems, advanced computer architectures, AI infrastructure, and long-cycle commercial relationships with demonstrated success expanding global businesses into new sectors.

Vachani most recently served as senior vice president, general manager, Automotive Business Unit for Arm Limited, a position she held from 2018 until 2026, where she successfully developed market specific IP programs into new, high-value recurring revenue streams. She also helped develop Arm Total Access and Arm Flexible Access, expanding IP utilization across the licensee base, and founded the SOAFEE Alliance, which today includes more than 200 member companies. From 2015 to 2018, Vachani was vice president, general manager of Intel Corporation’s Internet of Things Group. Prior to Intel, Vachani was vice president, general manager, Power, Lighting and Display at Skyworks Solutions beginning in 2013. Before Skyworks, Vachani held various program and product line positions at Texas Instruments, Inc. ending as vice president, general manager, Single Core Processors.

Vachani served as a member of the board of directors of Axcelis Technologies, Inc., a publicly traded semiconductor equipment manufacturer, from 2022 to 2025. Vachani earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Engineering from Texas A&M University and an Executive M.B.A. from The University of Texas at Austin.

The Board selected Vachani for her proven track record and commitment to innovation to build upon Adeia’s successful transformation. She will continue the focus on strengthening our technology leadership in the semiconductor and media markets, diversifying our recurring revenue streams beyond Pay-TV, identifying and investing in new growth areas, and fostering a culture that empowers our people to achieve the company’s long-term value creation goals.

“Dipti Vachani is the right leader for Adeia’s next chapter,” said Dan Moloney, chairman of the Board. “The Board’s Transition Committee conducted a rigorous search process and considered an exceptional field of candidates, and Vachani stood out for her ability to translate R&D capabilities and innovation roadmap into greater strategic relevance, new markets, stronger customer and ecosystem pull, and ultimately greater shareholder value. Our business today is positioned for continued revenue growth, led by an exceptional executive team with decades of experience and past successes. On behalf of the entire Board, I also want to thank Paul for four years of exceptional leadership and guidance; he leaves the company in a position of significant financial and strategic strength.”

# Adeia Names Dipti Vachani CEO as Paul Davis Steps Down

 September 29, 2026 

Dipti Vachani

Adeia Inc. has appointed semiconductor industry veteran Dipti Vachani as Chief Executive Officer, effective October 12, 2026, as the technology licensing company looks to expand its semiconductor and media businesses into new markets.

Vachani will also join Adeia’s board of directors on October 12. She succeeds Paul E. Davis, who informed the company in May that he planned to step down as CEO and a director to focus on his health and personal pursuits. Davis will remain an advisor through the end of 2026 to support the leadership transition.

Vachani brings nearly 30 years of semiconductor industry experience spanning intellectual property, computing architectures, AI infrastructure and global technology businesses. She most recently served as Senior Vice President and General Manager of Arm Limited’s Automotive Business Unit, a position she held from 2018 through 2026.

At Arm, Vachani developed market-specific intellectual property programs into recurring revenue streams and helped develop Arm Total Access and Arm Flexible Access, programs designed to broaden access to the company’s IP portfolio across its licensee base.

She also founded the SOAFEE Alliance, an automotive technology initiative that has grown to more than 200 member companies.

Before Arm, Vachani served from 2015 to 2018 as Vice President and General Manager of Intel Corp.’s Internet of Things Group. She previously led the Power, Lighting and Display business at Skyworks Solutions and held a series of program and product leadership positions at Texas Instruments, ultimately serving as Vice President and General Manager of Single Core Processors.

“Dipti Vachani is the right leader for Adeia’s next chapter,” said Dan Moloney, chairman of Adeia’s board. He said Vachani’s ability to translate research and development capabilities into new markets, customer relationships and commercial opportunities distinguished her during the board’s search process.

Her appointment comes as Adeia works to broaden the commercial reach of a licensing portfolio containing more than 14,250 patent assets worldwide.

The company develops and licenses technology rather than manufacturing end products, making the ability to convert research and intellectual property into long-term licensing relationships central to its business model.

Adeia’s semiconductor portfolio includes technologies such as 3D interconnect and hybrid bonding, along with advanced thermal management technologies aimed at increasingly demanding semiconductor and AI data center applications. Its media technologies cover areas including content discovery, personalization and streaming.

Under Vachani, the company plans to continue strengthening its positions in semiconductor and media technology while diversifying recurring revenue beyond Pay-TV and identifying additional markets for its intellectual property.

Vachani pointed to hybrid bonding and thermal technology for AI semiconductor infrastructure as potential growth areas, along with additional licensing opportunities in streaming, e-commerce and automotive markets.

“Adeia’s award-winning portfolio of more than 14,250 worldwide patent assets, its deep culture of invention, and the momentum the team has built provide a remarkable foundation for the company’s future,” Vachani said.

Her background at Arm is particularly relevant to Adeia’s licensing model. Arm has built its business around licensing processor architectures and related technology across a broad ecosystem, while Vachani’s automotive work involved developing market-specific IP programs and building relationships across technology suppliers and customers.
